scienceFacts: The speed of light is 299,792,458 meters per second.

Antibiotics only work against bacteria, not viruses.

Diamonds are made entirely of carbon atoms in a crystalline structure.
RNA plays a crucial role in protein synthesis within cells.
A black hole's gravity is so strong that not even light can escape.
The tallest mountain in the solar system is Olympus Mons on Mars.
Earth's core is mainly composed of iron and nickel.
Kepler’s laws describe the elliptical orbits of planets.
Photosynthesis converts carbon dioxide and sunlight into oxygen and glucose in plants.
Lightning bolts can reach temperatures hotter than the surface of the sun.
An octopus has three hearts, and its blood is blue due to copper-based hemocyanin.
The Hubble Space Telescope has provided detailed images of distant galaxies.
The human brain consumes about 20% of the body's total energy.
Tectonic plate movements cause earthquakes and volcanic activity.

The periodic table was first organized by Dmitri Mendeleev in 1869.
The Milky Way galaxy is estimated to contain over 100 billion stars.
A day on Venus is longer than a year on Venus due to its slow rotation.
The strong nuclear force holds atomic nuclei together.
Newton’s first law states that objects remain in motion unless acted upon by an external force.
Water is the only substance that exists in all three states naturally on Earth.

The sun's energy is generated by nuclear fusion, converting hydrogen into helium.
Earth’s atmosphere is composed of 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen, and trace gases.
The process of nuclear fission is used to generate power in reactors.
